title: Municipal accommodation tax corporation and surplus land plan
subtitle: Heritage designations, housing action plan, battery storage zoning, farmers market alcohol sampling, sidewalk tractor purchase and sight triangle by-law.
overview: Council approved a municipal service corporation structure for economic development and tourism, which would administer a future municipal accommodation tax. Staff will now begin community engagement, a required case study and draft incorporation documents, and will report back before the corporation is formally established. Council also approved additional project funding {{vote:m8}}.

After a closed session, the Mayor reported a resolution to categorize Township properties, begin declaring surplus properties, seek realtor services, set up a housing reserve fund and delegate sales authority to the Chief Administrative Officer. The minutes record no vote on it.

Council also gave notice of intent to designate three Fergus properties under the Ontario Heritage Act, committed to a Township housing action plan in the 2026 budget {{vote:m14}}, and passed the zoning by-law for a battery energy storage facility on Guelph Street {{vote:m15}}. Other approvals covered alcohol sampling at the Elora Farmers' Market, a sidewalk tractor purchase, a sight triangle by-law and a farm drainage shop rezoning. The meeting ran past its three-hour limit and was extended to 9 pm.

decisions.item: Municipal service corporation for tourism and economic development
decisions.detail: Council approved the proposed corporation structure, moving to engagement, a case study and draft documents, plus added project funding, with a report back before it is established {{vote:m8}}.

Council affirmed a defined Township role on housing and directed the 2026 budget to include an action plan, study of an advisory committee, county funding applications and staffing review {{vote:m14}}.
Council stated its notice of intent to designate the vacant stone farmhouse at 219 Farley Road under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m5}}.
Council stated its notice of intent to designate 300 St. Andrew Street West, noted in discussion as the first designated church in Fergus {{vote:m7}}.
Council gave three readings to a by-law rezoning part of 6235 Guelph Street to allow a battery energy storage facility, effective once the county plan amendment is in force {{vote:m15}}.
Council permitted vendor alcohol sampling in Bissell Park and delegated annual review of future requests to the Managing Director of Community Services {{vote:m10}}.
Council did not oppose demolishing the structures at 6518 First Line and approved removing the property from the heritage register beforehand {{vote:m12}}.
Council awarded a new articulated sidewalk tractor purchase at an upset limit of $186,173.74, funded early from the 2026 equipment reserve {{vote:m13}}.

debate: A delegate from the local heritage committee urged designating 219 Farley Road to prevent demolition by neglect, noting that designation does not freeze a property and can allow adaptive reuse. Councillors asked who would maintain the vacant building meanwhile; staff said designation adds property standards tools, and the owner can object.

One councillor said they were uncomfortable designating the farmhouse, questioning whether it was a pressing need and raising the tension between celebrating settler heritage and reconciliation. The delegate said designation criteria are provincial and that the Township is also working to recognize Indigenous and racialized communities' heritage.

On the municipal service corporation, councillors asked how council could step in if it disagreed with the corporation. The consultant pointed to the CAO's operational accountability, annual budget approval, quarterly reports and defined decision-making limits. Others asked for clear roles between community services and the new corporation, and for economic development not to be overshadowed by tourism.

A resident delegate on the accommodation tax urged faster short-term rental regulation and safety inspections following a recent fire. Council members noted short-term rental regulation is paused pending a workshop later this year, with hopes to advance it alongside the tax.

On housing, one councillor said they did not favour another committee, and staff clarified it would only be investigated. Staff said municipal incentives would need to grow to affect affordability, and noted the county funding for member municipalities.
